chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Hammad, from Shu'ayb, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

He was asked about eating garlic, onion, and leeks, so he said: 'There is no problem in eating them raw and in the pots, and there is no problem in being treated with garlic, but when one of you eats that, he should not go out to the Masjid.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating garlic and onions before going to the mosque?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that while the consumption of pungent vegetables like garlic, onion, and leeks is legally permissible (mubah) whether raw or cooked, the primary concern is social courtesy (adab) within the community. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on removing harm (darar) and preventing annoyance to others in shared sacred spaces, linking dietary habits directly to communal worship etiquette.
